CNTF binds to a cell surface receptor complex consisting of at least two subunits, one of which is a member of the cytokine receptor family, and that this receptor complex is present on a variety of neuronal cells, including embryonic and adult primary neurons.

the molecular mechanism(s), by which CNTFs influence the proliferation, survival and differentiation of cells.
the development of molecular probes for the CNTF receptor, the characterization of CNTF receptors, and the identification of CNTF-responsive cell types in the nervous system.
the development and application of novel molecular and cellular methods to identify, characterize, and clone genes encoding the functional receptor(s) for ciliary neuro-trophic factor (CNT F).

the receptor for CNTF is a heterodimer of gp140 and a 130-kDa protein that is expressed on a subset of neurons.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a functional receptor for CNTF on a variety of cell lines and primary neuronal cultures and have begun to identify the signaling pathway(s) that mediate the CNTF response.
we have developed a set of tools to identify and characterize cells and tissues that respond to CNTFs.

The main takeaway from our work is that
CNTF is a pleiotropic cytokine that is expressed in the developing nervous system and acts on a wide variety of cell types to promote cell survival.
CNTF receptors can be detected and separated from other cell-surface receptors by using a genetically engineered CFT molecule that contains an "epitpe tag" at its carboxy terminus.
